newsitem.title: FRANCE: French court rejects Herzog freedom bid.
newsitem.headline: French court rejects Herzog freedom bid.

text.p: A French court on Friday rejected a bid by Joel Herzog, son of former Israeli president Chaim Herzog, to be freed from custody during a probe into his suspected complicity with a casino sleaze scandal.
The court in the southern city of Aix-en-Provence ruled that Herzog, in detention since early December, should be held during the investigation.

Herzog, 47, is suspected of complicity in the payment of a 1.45 million franc ($290,000) bribe to Michel Mouillot, mayor of the French Riviera city of Cannes who is also in detention, the sources said.
Herzog, who is being held in Grasse prison nearby, normally resides in Switzerland and holds dual Israeli and British nationality.

He was placed under investigation as an associate of businessman Nissim Gaon whose empire includes the Noga-Hilton hotel in Cannes. The case involves a requested municipal permit to place an extra 100 slot machines in the Grand Riviera Casino inside the Noga-Hilton.
